# [Spec Decode][Perf] Support vocab-parallel DSpark top-k for DeepSeek V4

## Purpose

The existing `dspark_draft_topk` optimization limits each sequential DSpark
Markov projection to the top-k base-logit candidates, but it is currently
usable only by Qwen3's single-rank draft vocabulary. DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731
uses a full target vocabulary sharded across tensor-parallel ranks, so its
greedy DSpark path still all-gathers dense logits and evaluates the Markov
projection over the full vocabulary for every speculative step.

This change extends the opt-in path to DeepSeek-V4 DSpark:

- select top-k base logits locally on every vocabulary shard;
- all-gather only candidate values and global token IDs, then select the
  global top-k;
- gather the corresponding rows from the replicated Markov head and score
  only those candidates;
- sample the winning candidate sequentially, preserving the dependency on the
  previous draft token; and
- keep the existing dense path unchanged unless `dspark_draft_topk` is set.

For TP=8 and top-k=512, candidate communication is proportional to
`2 * k * TP` entries per row instead of the full 129,280-token vocabulary.
The new path is currently limited to greedy DeepSeek-V4 DSpark drafting; the
existing dense sampling path remains in use whenever draft logits are needed.

There is no linked issue.

## Duplicate-work check

Immediately before preparing this draft, open upstream PRs were searched for
`DeepSeek V4 DSpark topk`, `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`, `DSpark speculative
decoding`, and `sparse top-k draft logits`. No open PR implements this
vocab-parallel DeepSeek path.

- #49969 is the merged Qwen3 top-k implementation that this change extends.
  Its PR explicitly scoped support to Qwen3 and its dense top-k path assumes
  locally materialized draft logits.
- #50737 optimizes the exact dense Markov projection with in-place `addmm`.
  It is complementary, though it overlaps several DSpark files and may require
  rebasing.
- #51209 reuses sparse-attention indexer results across DeepSeek-V4 layers. It
  does not change DSpark vocabulary scoring or Markov projection.
- #53972 optimizes the initial DSpark mHC projection. It does not change draft
  logits or Markov scoring.
- #52165 changes DeepSeek-V4 DSpark checkpoint detection and overlaps the
  speculative configuration file, but it does not add a top-k execution path.

## Test plan and results

Focused tests on the rebased branch:

```text
<active-env>/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/test_config.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dspark_topk.py \
  -k 'draft_topk or gathered_markov or deepseek or vocab_parallel' -v

24 passed, 214 deselected
```

The tests cover configuration propagation, sparse scores versus dense scores,
the sequential previous-token dependency, and the case where top-k is larger
than one local vocabulary shard.

Relevant tests before the final rebase also passed:

```text
<active-env>/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_config.py -k dspark \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dspark_topk.py \
  tests/models/test_dspark_mla.py \
  tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py -q

35 passed, 228 deselected
```

Applicable checks passed on all changed files:

```text
pre-commit run ruff-format --files <changed files>
pre-commit run ruff-check --files <changed files>
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files <changed source files>
git diff --check
```

After rebasing to upstream commit `d1922cb5a7`, the exact model served on eight
H200 GPUs with TP=8, expert parallelism, FP8 KV cache, seven greedy DSpark
tokens, and `dspark_draft_topk=512`. A 32-request, 1024-input/128-output smoke
run completed 32/32 requests with no illegal memory access.

The submitted patch was also applied without conflicts to a local verification
branch at upstream commit `56058fd572`. Its stable patch ID exactly matches the
fork commit; the focused 24-test suite, mypy, commit hooks, and diff check were
rerun on that current-main verification head.

## H200 profile and serving A/B

The controlled A/B was collected on upstream commit `9236159bb6` before the
final rebase. Both arms used the same source and server configuration except
for `dspark_draft_topk=512` in the candidate:

```text
8 x NVIDIA H200, TP=8, expert parallelism
FP8 KV cache, DSpark with 7 speculative tokens, greedy drafting
max_num_batched_tokens=8192, max_num_seqs=256
1024 input tokens -> 128 output tokens
32 prompts, concurrency=32, ignore_eos, temperature=0
five steady-state measurements per arm
```

| Metric | Dense baseline | top-k=512 | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Output throughput | 830.80 token/s | 881.45 token/s | **+6.10%** |
| Per-run median TTFT | 493.38 ms | 461.62 ms | **-6.44%** |
| Per-run median TPOT | 23.50 ms | 23.02 ms | **-2.05%** |
| Draft acceptance | 47.66% | 51.36% | **+3.70 pp** |

For output throughput, an independent bootstrap with 200,000 resamples gave a
95% interval of `[+1.49%, +10.00%]`. The exact one-sided permutation p-value
was 0.01984 and the exact one-sided Mann-Whitney p-value was 0.04762.

This is an end-to-end result, not a pure kernel-time attribution. The candidate
also raised draft acceptance by 3.70 percentage points, so the measured gain
combines reduced computation/communication with the changed truncated proposal
distribution. A low-concurrency probe was noisy and did not establish a gain;
the feature therefore remains opt-in rather than becoming a default.

The TP8 trace attributed 59.71% of rank-0 GPU kernel time to communication and
showed 64 full-vocabulary all-gathers plus 224 sequential Markov projections in
the captured window. This optimization directly targets those two repeated
operations.

## Model evaluation

A paired GSM8K smoke evaluation used 100 questions, five-shot prompting,
greedy generation, at most 256 new tokens, and concurrency 32:

| Arm | Accuracy | Invalid rate |
|---|---:|---:|
| Dense baseline | 0.96 | 0.00 |
| top-k=512 | 0.96 | 0.00 |

Target-model verification remains unchanged, so speculative decoding preserves
the target distribution; this eval checks the concrete serving path for a
regression signal.

## AI-assistance and submitter review

AI assistance was used for profiling, implementation, testing, benchmarking,
statistical analysis, and drafting this description.

- [x] The human submitter reviewed every changed line.
- [x] The human submitter understands and can defend the implementation and
  all reported measurements.
- [x] Duplicate-work checks were rerun immediately before publication.
- [x] The final commit contains no private benchmark artifacts or generated
  files.
